responses.overview: {{project_name}} is architected as a modern web application with a clear client-server separation. The frontend is a single-page application communicating with a RESTful API backend. Real-time features (team availability, handoff notifications) are delivered via WebSocket connections. The system is designed for horizontal scalability, with stateless application servers behind a load balancer and a managed PostgreSQL database for persistence. Timezone calculations are centralized in a dedicated service module to ensure correctness and testability.

tech_stack.rationale: Server-side rendering for SEO and initial load performance. TypeScript provides type safety across the frontend codebase. Strong ecosystem of compatible libraries and active community.

tech_stack.choice: Tailwind CSS with Radix UI primitives
tech_stack.rationale: Tailwind enables rapid iteration on design without context-switching to CSS files. Radix provides accessible, unstyled primitives for complex components like date pickers and dropdowns.

High-performance async framework with automatic OpenAPI documentation. Python has excellent timezone handling libraries (pytz, zoneinfo). Type hints align with Pydantic for request/response validation.
Robust timezone-aware datetime types (TIMESTAMPTZ). JSONB support for flexible schema evolution. Strong indexing capabilities for query performance. Proven at scale.
Mature ORM with excellent PostgreSQL support. Async session support aligns with FastAPI's async architecture. Alembic for migration management.
WebSocket provides low-latency bidirectional communication for live availability updates. Redis Pub/Sub enables broadcasting across multiple application server instances.
Handles background tasks: notification delivery, digest generation, calendar sync polling. Redis serves double duty as cache and message broker.
Standard library module using the IANA timezone database. No third-party dependency for core timezone logic. Automatically updated via system package manager.
Managed authentication reduces security surface area. Supports OAuth for third-party integrations (Google Calendar, Slack). SSO support for enterprise customers.

infrastructure.hosting: AWS ECS Fargate for containerized application services. RDS PostgreSQL for managed database. ElastiCache Redis for caching and pub/sub. S3 for file storage. CloudFront CDN for static assets.
infrastructure.ci_cd: GitHub Actions for CI/CD pipeline. Automated testing on pull requests. Staging deployment on merge to develop branch. Production deployment on release tags with manual approval gate.
infrastructure.monitoring: Datadog for application metrics, distributed tracing, and log aggregation. PagerDuty for on-call alerting. Sentry for frontend and backend error tracking. Custom dashboard for timezone-specific operational metrics.
infrastructure.estimated_cost: Development phase: ~$200/month (minimal infrastructure). Launch phase (up to 1000 users): ~$800/month. Growth phase (up to 10,000 users): ~$2,500/month. Costs scale primarily with database size and real-time connection count.

security_considerations: All API endpoints require authentication via JWT with short-lived access tokens and refresh token rotation
OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for all third-party integrations, with scoped permissions requesting minimal access
Calendar data is processed in memory and not persisted beyond the sync operation — only free/busy status is stored
Row-level security in PostgreSQL ensures organization data isolation at the database level
Rate limiting on all public-facing endpoints: 100 requests/minute for authenticated users, 10/minute for unauthenticated
Input validation via Pydantic models on all API endpoints, with strict type coercion disabled
WebSocket connections authenticated via token in the initial handshake, with periodic re-authentication
All sensitive configuration via environment variables, never committed to version control
responses.scalability_notes: The architecture supports horizontal scaling at every layer. Application servers are stateless — session data is stored in Redis, enabling seamless load balancing. PostgreSQL handles read scaling via read replicas; write scaling is addressed by table partitioning on organization_id if needed. Redis Pub/Sub enables WebSocket broadcasting across multiple server instances. The timezone calculation engine is CPU-bound but lightweight — overlap computations for a 100-person team complete in under 50ms. The primary scaling bottleneck is expected to be WebSocket connection count, addressable by dedicated WebSocket server instances behind a connection-aware load balancer.
responses.deployment_strategy: Docker containers orchestrated via ECS Fargate. Blue-green deployments for zero-downtime releases. Database migrations run as a pre-deployment step with automatic rollback on failure. Feature flags via LaunchDarkly for gradual rollout of new capabilities. Separate staging environment mirroring production topology for integration testing. Infrastructure defined as code via Terraform.

responses.overview: {{project_name}} follows a modular monolith architecture, optimized for development velocity and operational simplicity at early scale. The application is structured as a single deployable unit with well-defined internal module boundaries, making it straightforward to extract services later if scaling demands it. The core innovation — timezone-aware workflow primitives — is encapsulated in a dedicated domain module that all other modules depend on.

tech_stack.rationale: React's component model suits the interactive timezone visualizations. Vite provides fast development builds. TypeScript ensures type safety across the frontend.
Utility-first approach accelerates UI development. Consistent design tokens via configuration. Small production bundle via PurgeCSS.
Shared TypeScript types between frontend and backend eliminate schema drift. Excellent WebSocket support via Socket.io. Rich npm ecosystem for timezone handling (Luxon, date-fns-tz).
Type-safe database queries via Prisma. Automatic migration generation. PostgreSQL's TIMESTAMPTZ ensures correct timezone storage.
Mature WebSocket library with automatic fallback to long-polling. Room-based broadcasting maps naturally to team channels. Client-side reconnection handling built in.
TypeScript-native job queue. Scheduled jobs for digest generation. Retry logic with exponential backoff for integration sync.
Built on the Intl API and ICU timezone data. Handles DST transitions, half-hour offsets, and locale-aware formatting. No separate timezone database dependency.
Flexible authentication middleware. JWT for stateless API authentication. Extensible to support OAuth providers for SSO.

security_considerations: JWT tokens with 15-minute expiry and secure HTTP-only refresh cookies
Prisma parameterized queries prevent SQL injection by default
Input validation via Zod schemas on all API endpoints
CORS restricted to known frontend origins
Workspace-scoped data access enforced at the query layer — every database query includes workspace_id filter
OAuth tokens for third-party integrations encrypted at rest using AES-256
WebSocket authentication via token verification on connection upgrade
Dependency vulnerability scanning via GitHub Dependabot and npm audit in CI
responses.scalability_notes: The modular monolith starts as a single process handling HTTP, WebSocket, and background jobs. At scale, these can be separated: dedicated WebSocket servers for real-time presence, separate worker processes for background jobs (digests, sync), and multiple API server instances behind a load balancer. PostgreSQL connection pooling via PgBouncer handles database connection scaling. The timezone calculation module is stateless and CPU-bound — it scales linearly with application instances. Redis handles pub/sub for cross-instance WebSocket broadcasting. Expected bottleneck at scale is WebSocket connection count, addressable by Socket.io's Redis adapter for multi-server broadcasting.
responses.deployment_strategy: Containerized via Docker. Initial deployment as a single container on Railway with zero-config PostgreSQL and Redis. Database migrations via Prisma migrate, run as a release command before the new version starts. Feature flags via environment variables for progressive rollout. Health check endpoint at /health for load balancer integration. Automatic rollback if health check fails within 60 seconds of deployment.
